title: Power Up Safely This School Year
summary: Southern California Edison reminds students who are headed back to campus to keep electrical and fire safety in mind.
body_markdown:
In the age of electronics, students are heading to college campuses with more electrical and battery-powered devices than ever.


As part of[Campus Fire Safety Month](https://www.nfpa.org/education-and-research/building-and-life-safety/campus-and-dorm-fires) , dorm electrical safety and proper handling of lithium-ion batteries should be some of the first lessons students learn this semester.


September is a peak month for campus fires. From 2020 to 2024,[U.S. fire departments responded to over 3,000 structure fires in dormitories and other student housing](https://www.nfpa.org/education-and-research/building-and-life-safety/campus-and-dorm-fires) , including fires caused by lithium-ion batteries often found in laptops, phones, e-bikes and e-scooters.


When damaged, improperly charged or exposed to extreme temperatures, these batteries can overheat, catch fire or even explode,[resulting in serious injury or death](https://www.nfpa.org/education-and-research/building-and-life-safety/campus-and-dorm-fires) . Of fires reported to[The Center for Campus Fire Safety](https://www.myccfs.org/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=138:li-data-intro&catid=20:site-content&Itemid=210) , 11% resulted in injuries requiring medical attention, respiratory treatment or post-incident counseling services.
